endpoint: Investigator-assessed progression-free survival (PFS-INV)
result: Tafa-Len-R-CHOP vs R-CHOP: PFS HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.59-0.96), p=0.0194; median follow-up 35.2 months (EHA 2026 plenary).
quote: the trial met its primary endpoint of progression-free survival (PFS) by investigator assessment.
notes: Topline date 2026-01-05 comes from a TargetedOnc article of that date citing the Incyte release of the same day (Incyte's January release itself not opened). Primary endpoint met statement confirmed in Incyte's 30 May 2026 release (ASCO 2026 / The Lancet); full numbers at the EHA plenary on 13 June 2026. Registry PCD is 2026-09, so it is not clear whether the analysis was labelled interim or primary.

endpoint: Progression-free survival, pirtobrutinib+VenR vs VenR (IRC-assessed per release)
result: Topline: statistically significant, clinically meaningful PFS improvement; later reported 45% reduction in risk of progression or death (HR about 0.55), median follow-up 27.3 months.
quote: The study met its primary endpoint.
notes: Lilly topline release 2026-04-13 (BRUIN CLL-322 named): PFS by blinded IRC; HR/CI/p not given in the topline. The 45% risk reduction comes from a 15 June 2026 report (likely EHA 2026). OS immature. The release does not say whether the analysis was interim.

endpoint: Overall survival, serplulimab+chemo vs atezolizumab+chemo
result: Median OS 12.4 vs 10.2 months; 24-month OS 32.2% vs 17.6%; median follow-up 14.1 months; no HR, CI or p-value reported in sources found.
quote: 斯鲁利单抗组中位总生存期(OS)为12.4个月，优于阿替利珠单抗组的10.2个月
notes: ASTRIDE results are to be (or were) presented as an ESMO 2026 oral; first seen in Chinese financial media on 2026-10-19 (ESMO preview). The sources call ASTRIDE a US head-to-head bridging trial and describe the survival benefit as 'significant' (生存获益显著), but give no HR/p-value, no design (non-inferiority vs superiority) and no statement that the primary endpoint was met. ESMO abstract and Henlius release not accessed (10jqka page refused, robots). Needs re-check against the ESMO 2026 abstract.

endpoint: Progression-free survival, MeziKd vs Kd (phase 3 portion)
result: HR 0.48, p<0.0001; median PFS 18.0 vs 8.3 months; median follow-up 10.6 months (ASCO 2026).
quote: met its primary end point of a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement PFS
notes: BMS topline 2026-03-09 (date from TargetedOnc, which cites the BMS release of that day; BMS release not opened). Result came from an interim analysis that declared the primary endpoint met (rule 5). Two-stage design: the randomized phase 3 stage's PFS counts (rule 3a). Numbers from the ASCO 2026 report; 95% CI not given in that source.

endpoint: Co-primary: non-vellus TAHC change and subject self-assessment of hair coverage at 6 months
result: TAHC significant (p<0.05) in both SCALP 1 and SCALP 2 (539% and 168% relative improvement vs vehicle, not attributed); PRO significant in only one unnamed study.
quote: One study PRO endpoint reached statistical significance and the other study PRO showed a positive trend.
notes: Cosmo topline (ad hoc) 2025-12-03 reports SCALP 1 and SCALP 2 together without saying which study had which TAHC figure or which study's PRO reached significance. A later Cosmo release says efficacy was assessed with 'co-primary endpoints that incorporated both objective and patient-reported measures', so rule 3c applies: one of the two sister trials missed the PRO co-primary, but the sources do not say which. For SCALP 1 the outcome is therefore undetermined (yes if it is the study with significant PRO, no otherwise). Treated as vague under rule 9 (sister-trial result not separable). TAHC co-primary met in SCALP 1. Fiercepharma refused (client error); barchart URL too long to fetch.

endpoint: Percent change in body weight at week 80 (AHI in OSA subset not reported)
result: Week 80 (efficacy estimand): -12.7% (4 mg), -19.1% (9 mg), -20.8% (12 mg) vs -4.0% placebo; p-values not given.
quote: In both studies, retatrutide met the primary endpoint, delivering substantial weight loss.
notes: Lilly topline release 2026-07-23 for TRIUMPH-2 and TRIUMPH-3 reported separately. The second registered primary (AHI in the GSA2 OSA subset) is not reported; met decided by Lilly's statement that the primary endpoint was met (rule 3d). All three doses better than placebo; A1C was a key secondary.

endpoint: Percent change in EASI at week 8 (Part 2, HY209 gel 1% and 2% vs placebo)
result: Difference vs placebo did not reach the prespecified two-sided 0.025 significance level; placebo EASI improvement 58.1%; p-value not given.
quote: 누겔 투여군과 위약군 간 1차 평가지표 차이가 사전에 설정된 통계적 유의수준(양측성 0.025)을 충족하지 못한 것으로 확인됐다.
notes: Shaperon global phase 2b of Nugel (HY209 gel), Part 1 (dose-ranging, 33 pts) and Part 2 (175 pts). Topline filing (공시) reported by Hankyung and MT as 24 June 2026; Dailypharm says data arrived after market close on 23 June and were disclosed the same day, so the date may be 2026-06-23. Primary EASI endpoint not met in either part per Dailypharm (1 Oct 2026); some secondary endpoints p=0.044. Filing itself not read.

endpoint: Maintenance of body weight reduction at week 112, tirzepatide 5 mg and MTD vs placebo
result: Week 112 weight change: MTD -21.9%, 5 mg -16.6%, placebo -9.9%; ETD -12.0% (MTD) and -6.6% (5 mg), p<0.0001 (Lancet 2026).
quote: both Zepbound MTD and Zepbound 5 mg met the primary and all key secondary endpoints
notes: First disclosure found is Lilly's 12 May 2026 release with the ECO 2026 presentation and The Lancet publication; no earlier topline found. Lilly and the paper phrase the endpoint as percent change in body weight at week 112 rather than 'percent maintenance' as registered, but Lilly states the primary endpoint was met. Both arms met.

endpoint: Time to second day with GTC seizure over 24-week double-blind period
result: Median 141 vs 47 days (opakalim vs placebo); 33% vs 0% finished double-blind without a second GTC seizure; n=27 (15 vs 12); no formal statistical testing.
quote: Despite the limited enrollment, opakalim demonstrated a notable efficacy signal.
notes: Biohaven release 2026-05-26 (R&D Day) identifies the study by NCT06425159: closed before the prespecified sample size because of enrollment difficulties and portfolio prioritization. Biohaven gives descriptive primary-endpoint results and says 'Formal statistical testing is not provided', and makes no statement on whether the primary endpoint was met. Because an efficacy result was given, it is labelled vague rather than stopped_without_result. Quote is from Pharmacally's report of the release.

endpoint: PANSS total at 6 weeks (also EEG and smooth-pursuit eye tracking)
result: Interim, n=16 (8 vs 8): PANSS total -11.9 vs -5.6 (difference -6.3), no p-value; positive subscale p=0.01; EEG gamma/alpha power p=0.002-0.042.
quote: demonstrated trends indicative of improvement in positive and negative symptoms
notes: Prespecified interim analysis of 16 of 32 enrolled at SIRS 2026 (26 March 2026); the trial was continuing. The interim neither declared the primary endpoint met nor stopped the trial (rule 5); labelled reported/vague because numbers on the primary PANSS measure were released without a test. Corrected release (27 March) changed the PANSS figures from -11.1 vs -5.5. EEG was treated as pharmacodynamic, not efficacy (rule 2); eye tracking not reported. No final results found by 2026-10-28.

endpoint: Change in cardiac troponin T and CK-MB at 24 hours
result: Median cTnT rose about 129% (25 ug/kg) and 65% (75 ug/kg) vs about 615% with placebo; no p-values; CK-MB 24 h not reported.
quote: The Phase 2a study was primarily designed to establish safety and tolerability and explore preliminary efficacy signals
notes: ResoTher release 2026-09-14, headlined 'strong phase 2a results ... efficacy signals pointing to less cardiac injury'. It says the study 'was therefore not statistically powered to demonstrate efficacy' and gives only numerical biomarker patterns ('encouraging signals'), with no statement on the primary endpoints.

endpoint: Change in functional capacity, baseline to week 24
quote: Individual biomarker and efficacy data remain confidential pending potential publication in early 2026.
notes: Thiogenesis reported 'positive interim' results from its EU placebo-controlled MELAS phase 2 (9 patients, Radboud and CHU Angers) on 2025-11-04, with no primary-endpoint data. At Mitocon (2026-01-23) it reported interim MFIS fatigue improvement (up to 10% vs placebo, p<0.001). That trial is probably this one, but the release calls it single-blind while the registry says double-blind. Functional capacity (the registered primary) is not reported and neither interim declared it met, so per rule 5 this is reported = no. If the 'positive interim' wording is counted, first_public_date would be 2025-11-04 (vague). No final results found.

endpoint: Change in HbA1c from baseline to week 36
result: HbA1c reduction (efficacy estimand): 2.37% (2 mg), 2.67% (4 mg) vs 0.36% placebo; treatment-regimen estimand 2.19%/2.50% vs 0.66%; p-values not given.
quote: 主要终点及所有关键次要终点均达到优效。
notes: Hengrui announcement of 20 July 2026 on HRS9531-302 (ruipupotide) in treatment-naive Chinese T2DM, 218 participants, 2:1:2:1 randomization. Date taken from a 10jqka headline URL (page refused, robots) and the Gelonghui report ('7月20日'). Hengrui's own filing not read.

endpoint: Change in HbA1c from baseline to week 20, SHR-3167 vs insulin glargine
notes: Two searches (Chinese and English) found no public result for this phase 2. Only registry copies and a later SHR-3167 titration trial (NCT07472725) came up.

endpoint: Percent change in body weight and proportion with >=5% weight loss (registered at week 36)
quote: 获得积极顶线结果，达成主要终点及所有关键次要终点
notes: BrightGene SSE voluntary announcement No. 2026-029 (BGM0504-III-WL, 652 non-diabetic adults, 41 centres). The filing ID and Gelonghui give 5 May 2026; the document is dated 6 May. Timepoint discrepancy: the packet registers week 36, but the announcement reports weight at week 52 as the main analysis and gives no week-36 weight data. It says the primary endpoint and all key secondary endpoints were met. If a reviewer treats the week-52 reporting as a changed primary, the label would be endpoint_changed (rule 8).

endpoint: HBsAg <LOD (0.05 IU/mL) and HBV DNA <LLOQ (complete response)
result: Part A (AHB-137 300 mg vs placebo 4:1, per-protocol n=31): CR at end of treatment 68% (17/25) with AHB-137; placebo results and p-value not reported.
quote: In total, 68% of participants (17 of 25) achieved CR at EOT.
notes: EASL Congress 2026 (27-30 May, Qiu Y et al.) as reported by AJMC on 28 May 2026, which names NCT06829329. The abstract may have been online slightly earlier. Only Part A (monotherapy vs placebo) of an ongoing study is reported, descriptively, with no comparison or statement on the primary endpoint. The NA-combination part is not reported. Headline wording: 'high cure rates'.

endpoint: Change from baseline in DAS28-CRP at week 12
notes: Two searches found only registry copies and an ACR 2025 phase 1 healthy-volunteer abstract for BGB-45035 (acrabstracts.org/?p=43928). No phase 2 RA result found.

endpoint: EASI-75 and IGA response at week 24
notes: Two searches found MG-K10 phase 3 / 52-week data and the NMPA NDA acceptance, which come from other trials, but no result for this phase 2 (24-week EASI-75/IGA).

endpoint: Change in weekly average NRS pain score at week 6
quote: 基于该试验的积极结果，TRD205已被中国国家药品监督管理局药品审评中心(CDE)纳入突破性治疗药物名单。
notes: Sino Biopharmaceutical (Beijing Tide's parent) HKEX announcement of 14 July 2026 on the CDE breakthrough-therapy designation says it was based on 'positive results' of the completed phase 2 in chronic post-surgical neuropathic pain. No primary NRS result, dose or test is given. Announcement text read only through secondary reports; the 10jqka page was refused (robots).

endpoint: Change in peak FEV1 from baseline to week 4
quote: 乾粉吸入粉雾剂的2期临床试验亦获得了积极的顶线数据。
notes: On 7 Sept 2026 (ERS 2026 phase 1 data release) Sino Biopharm said the TQC3721 dry-powder-inhaler phase 2 'also obtained positive topline data', with no endpoint or statistics. On 13 July 2026 (AstraZeneca licensing deal) the DPI phase 2 was still described as ongoing, so the first statement falls between those dates and may be slightly earlier than 7 Sept.

endpoint: Semen volume and sperm count at 90 and 180 minutes
result: Company reports the pill prevented sperm release in all participants within two hours; no numbers, placebo comparison or statistics given.
quote: Prevented sperm release in all participants within two hours
notes: News reports (IFLScience 31 Aug 2026; La Voce di New York 27 Sept 2026) describe a small randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 of NEXT Life Sciences' on-demand 'PausePill'. That it is NLS-133 is inferred: NLS-133 is the company's on-demand pill, whose phase 2 evaluated semen after dosing (FemTech Insider, Feb 2026). The results are unpublished. There is no statement on the registered semen-volume/sperm-count endpoints and no test.

endpoint: Change in Brief Fatigue Inventory score over 12 weeks
quote: The success of Phase 3 of the Randomised Clinical Trial (RCT) of Nuvastatic
notes: Bernama (21 May 2026, citing Malaysia's ministry KPKM) and an investigator's LinkedIn post (29 June 2026, MASCC) describe a 'successful' phase 3 of Nuvastatic in breast cancer patients but give no endpoint, numbers or test. A sister phase 3 in triple-negative breast cancer (NCT07669467) exists. Bernama says 'advanced-stage breast cancer patients undergoing treatment', while this trial lists adjuvant chemotherapy, so attribution to this trial is uncertain.

endpoint: Proportion with IGF-1 index <=1.0 at week 12, SYHX2008 vs Sandostatin LAR
notes: CSPC voluntary announcement of 18 June 2026 (US FDA IND clearance in acromegaly) says only that the product 'has entered Phase III clinical trials in China', with no phase 2 efficacy result. Two searches found nothing else.
